q: The revolutionaries of this period, rather than attempting a violent mass revolution or subverting army loyalty, chose to follow the methods of:
Jatindranath Mukherjee, popularly known as Bagha Jatin, led which revolutionary group and organised the 'German Plot' (Zimmerman Plan) to import arms during World War I?
Bagha Jatin's call "We shall die to awaken the nation" is associated with his final confrontation with police, which occurred at:
o: Balasore, on the Orissa coast, in September 1915

q: Which of the following describes a key limitation of Bengal's revolutionary movement, as noted in the chapter's evaluation?
o: It received full support from the Muslim League throughout
It had no impact whatsoever on the educated youth
It successfully mobilised the peasantry across Bengal
Overemphasis on Hindu religious symbolism kept Muslims aloof, and its narrow upper-caste social base excluded mass participation

q: In Punjab, extremism was fuelled by frequent famines, rising land revenue and irrigation tax, and the zamindars' practice of:
Ajit Singh (Bhagat Singh's uncle) organised the extremist Anjuman-i-Mohisban-i-Watan in Lahore, bringing out which journal?
Shyamji Krishnavarma founded the Indian Home Rule Society ('India House') in London in 1905, along with which journal?
The Ghadr Party, organised around a weekly newspaper by the same name, had its headquarters at:
The Berlin Committee for Indian Independence, established in 1915 with German foreign office support under the 'Zimmerman Plan', included which of the following founders?
o: Virendranath Chattopadhyay, Bhupendranath Dutta and Lala Hardayal

q: The mission led by Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh, Barkatullah and Obaidullah Sindhi to Kabul during World War I aimed to:
o: Negotiate a treaty between Afghanistan and British India
Recruit Afghan soldiers for the British Indian Army
Organise a 'provisional Indian government' with the help of Crown Prince Amanullah
Establish a Ghadr Party branch in Afghanistan

q: The mutiny at Singapore on February 15, 1915, involving the Punjabi Muslim 5th Light Infantry and the 36th Sikh battalion, was led by:
o: Jamadar Chisti Khan, Jamadar Abdul Gani and Subedar Daud Khan
Kartar Singh Saraba and Bhagwan Singh

q: Which of the following factors contributed to the temporary decline in revolutionary activity after the First World War?
o: Total absence of any nationalist sentiment after 1917
Release of prisoners under the Defence of India Rules, Montagu's August 1917 statement promising constitutional reforms, and the arrival of Gandhi with a non-violent programme
Permanent alliance between revolutionaries and the British government
Complete elimination of all revolutionary leaders
